N-5.confirmedByCopy: 19.11./20.11., Copy (now nuovasolution-71): the capital goes by position, so whichever part comes first takes it. Recorded in §2.3 of the same file, commit fb2e600. The two sentences above are therefore criteria, not my interpretation.

N-5.myReading: 'capital letter only on the first part' is a rule about position, not a description of the two literals: whichever part comes first takes the capital. The other reading produces a sentence starting lower-case, which no editor wants.

foldAndNothingLost.mechanism: components/home/plan-card-fold.tsx keeps the groups in the document at every width and only folds them on the phone (globals.css .plans-card-fold); at ≥ 640 px they stand open and the button is hidden
foldAndNothingLost.whyThisMattersToMyMethod: textContent includes display:none text, so my sentence comparison sees the folded groups and 'nothing lost' passes. scrollHeight excludes them, so the depth really falls. Both of my methods behave correctly here - the fold is a genuine fix, not a way around my metrics.
foldAndNothingLost.butThereforeNotEnough: 'nothing lost' by the document alone would also pass if the core of the offer were folded away. So Copy §3's visible-while-closed list is a SECOND, stricter criterion, measured as actually painted elements at 390 with the fold closed: the plan name and the 'for whom' line, both ways each with its line under the button, and the pilot line above the plans.
foldAndNothingLost.codeState: clean - aria-expanded, aria-controls, an aria-label per plan, the body always in the document. The 44 px tap height is in CSS and gets measured on the build.
